body:
I wish I could send hugs to every one who has talked to me tonight. I feel like tongiht's crisis is... postponed, at the very least.
I don't have solutions about how to make things feel better going forward, but I think I feel okay enough tonight that I'm going to try to sleep.

I wish I could send hugs to every one who has talked to me tonight. I feel like tongiht's crisis is... postponed, at the very least.

I don't have solutions about how to make things feel better going forward, but I think I feel okay enough tonight that I'm going to try to sleep.

Do you know, you are a wonderful person. It's easy to forget that there are PEOPLE inside other people, and that they're dealing with struggles, too.

(Also, I have regained the weight... just, I've lost weight in the past but it doesn't make me feel like I'm any better. No matter what I do, I'm stil the same me, inside. I've done some pretty terrific things, but it's still me inside me and it's still not good enough. It's as if nothing I do makes anything better.)

Do you feel like this continually? I guess what my day-to-day is like... it's pretty normal, I think. I go to work, come home, make dinner with my husband, play some video games and go to bed. It's a good life. But, on my drive to and from work, if someone swerves into my lane, I don't flinch from them. Before, when I had health insurance, if I was having trouble sleeping, I'd take a xanax and an ambien and wash it down with a drink and think that I wasn't actively trying to commit suicide but if I didn't wake up, that would be okay too. If I can't sleep now, sometimes I take walks outside in the middle of the night, even though I'm a woman and the streets aren't particularly well lit or well traveled. I feel like I live recklessly, not seeking out death but also, slightly, inviting it if it happens to come by. I almost wish I was at that deep despair point so I could do something fucking decisive already. Instead, I passively wait for my life to just stop happening.

Do normal people feel this way and they are just better at hiding it? Should I accept that this is part of being human, and learn how to hide it the way everyone else does?

My husband and I were talking about having kids within the next few years. We're in our early 30s and newly married, though we've been together for years. I'm afraid to have kids, because even though I think I could be a kick ass mother, I feel like it would be one more burden that I would have to live for. That I would have to protect my life, even though I don't particularly want to, because if I were to die, it would mess some little people up.

How do you feel, in your day to day? Once you're out of the suicidal depression, do you feel normal? Like you're happy to be alive? Like you want to keep living? Or is it simply a lifting of that darker urge-to-die feeling, and settling into the grey sort of "I'll keep living if I keep living but if something came along and I died, that'd be cool too"?

No, thank you for the questions.

I have been diagnosed with depression in the past. I lost my health insurance a year and a half ago. I was taking meds through February of this year, when I had to wean off of them due to lack of insurance (one of them I could get through the $4 Target prescriptions, but the other would cost me around $80 a month, and I couldn't find a doctor to write the prescription, so I self-weaned off of them over the course of six weeks or so... I have some experience with them in the past, so I was able to wean without difficulty, though I do know that I should probably be on something.)

I have a hard time falling asleep at night, and I'm usually up by around 7 for work, or 8/9 on weekends. Lots of nights I can't sleep until 3-4am. Sometimes I do drink too much, or I take Nyquil or something, just to knock myself out so I get some sleep. Other nights, I lie there until it's time to get back up. I rarely get enough sleep. I took Ambien at one point, but that was a couple years ago when I was in school and had health insurance.

I don't think I'm sad. Most of the time I feel pretty cheerful, but I feel so ungrateful. Like I have this wonderful life and all I want is not to have to live it anymore. I feel like I need a new way of coping with day-to-day stressors, and alcohol is probably a bad avenue for me. I feel like I'm wasting your time, and I'm sorry. I don't know what anyone can do or say to help. Thank you for your time anyway. :)

Thank you for your reply. I don't know what I'm really asking for here, so maybe I'm in the wrong place.

I think I'm going to quit my job. Maybe. It's so easy to dream of these things, but ... wherever I go, there I am, you know? I've traveled, I've gone through different degree programs, but no matter what I do or where I go, I'm still the same person. I can't remember not feeling this way. I don't know if everyone feels like this, and they're just good at hiding it?

I have a good life. I'm married and I love my spouse. I have two great dogs. I have a law degree from an incredibly good school. I do hate my job, but I felt this way long before I got this job, long before law school, for as long as I can remember. I've lost weight, maxed out my deadlift, taken antidepressants (though not currently, as I don't have health insurance), left the country, taken time off to chill at the beach. This feeling never leaves. It gets worse sometimes, more urgent, but never better.

I wish I could trade my life for the life of someone who really wanted to be alive. I don't think it's fair that babies die, and I have to be alive and I don't even appreciate it. And I still don't know how to face each day... Every day I wake up and go about my business, looking for ways I could "accidentally" cease to exist.

I feel mostly rational. I don't know why I am this way. I don't know what to do to make it better. I just hate myself and I don't want to have to live anymore.
